newsitem.title: UK: Lacklustre LME copper edges down as spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: Lacklustre LME copper edges down as spreads widen.

text.p: Copper prices drifted back from early highs on the London Metal Exchange on Monday, but increasingly tight spreads showed no sign of narrowing, traders said.

Cash to three months backwardation came out some $15 to $315/$320, and cash for a day ratched up to $23/$24 as the first of the tight dates, January 29, came into play. The LME has imposed a limit of one percent of cash, which on Monday was $25.
"Tomorrow we're going to see it at the limit," one trader said.
The market was focusing on whether shorts would cover or roll over and thereby how much the spreads would lose steam as the tight dates became prompt.

Feb/threes backwardation bucked the trend by easing from as high as $87 in the morning to around $81 by the end of the kerb. Talk had circulated that interest in the Feb/threes was due to a player covering February option positions.
But three months activity was muted, and an early push above $2,260 per tonne fizzled out despite flaring spreads. Copper finished the afternoon kerb at $2,247, up just $4 from Friday's kerb close.
LME stocks were expected to rise by about 8,000 tonnes on Tuesday, which may have helped depress prices, some traders said. Last Friday stocks rose a hefty 12,775 tonnes.
"People say it'll be 6,000 tonnes up in Europe and another 2,000 in the U.S." a trader said.
Aluminium finished slightly stronger at $1,641, a $5 increase from Friday and just above key resistance at $1,640.
Spreads also held top billing with aluminium. But unlike in copper the cash/threes contango widened slightly to $22/$21, compared to $20/$17 earlier in the day.
Nickel at $7,300 and zinc at $1,139 were unchanged from Friday's kerb closes.
Lead eased $2 to $697, failing to maintain a grip above $700.
Tin drifted $30 lower to $5,990, while alloy was last quoted $6 firmer at $1,538/39.
